correctness.rationale: Re-audited the replacement RESULT.md. The frozen Finding misleadingly says ordinary kernel-sign indicators attain the operator norm: for any row of signed mass one and absolute mass R, its largest absolute output on indicators is (R+1)/2, strictly smaller than the maximizing norm in this problem. The repaired statement explicitly distinguishes signed ±1 inputs for the norm from indicators for the one-sided extrema. Decomposing the affine range into the two layer indicators and centered coordinate contrasts gives contrast covariance H/[n(n−1)] and the two stated kernel rows. Only disjoint pair–pair entries can change sign within a layer; n=3 has none. The increasing/decreasing row functions cross uniquely at the uniform-atom weight. The conditional Bernoulli ratio and stationary, strictly log-concave determinant check also hold. No change to the supporting computation was needed.
residual_risks: Exact Gram checks are finite and were inspected, not rerun; the analytic proof establishes the full parameter range. The excluded probability endpoints are not part of the theorem.

value.rationale: This solves a natural one-parameter robustness-design problem on the first two nonzero Boolean layers. The full formulas locate both the disjoint-entry sign threshold and the actual worst-row transition, identify the unique minimax design, and quantify sharp nonpositivity for bounded inputs. The value is the weighted behavior and unique optimum, not the single uniform benchmark or the determinant comparison.
residual_risks: No minimization over arbitrary nonexchangeable measures or arbitrary projections is asserted.
